x: Polylogue is an app for Mastodon and compatible servers. Mastodon is a social network made of many independent servers that talk to each other, often called the Fediverse. Your account lives on one server; Polylogue is the window you use it through.
An iPhone or iPad with iOS or iPadOS 18 or later, or a Mac with macOS 15 or later. An account on a Mastodon-compatible server, unless you only want to try the demo.

It translates the posts you read, and lets you write a reply in your own language, check the translation and publish it. Translation uses Apple's Translation framework on your device. AI translation is an optional extra that you set up yourself. Polylogue's own menus and buttons are in English.

c: Chapter 2: Sign in or try the demo
x: Open Polylogue. Under Your Mastodon server, enter your server's address, for example mastodon.social. Choose Continue with Mastodon. Your web browser opens your server's sign-in page. Sign in there and allow Polylogue to use your account. The browser returns you to Polylogue, which opens your Home timeline. Your password is entered only on your server. Polylogue keeps the access token it receives in the Keychain, and you stay signed in until you sign out. If you see Your saved session expired. Please sign in again., repeat these steps.

c: Chapter 2: Sign in or try the demo
x: Choose Explore with a demo account on the sign-in screen to look around with sample posts. Nothing you do is published. To leave, open Preferences and choose Sign Out.

c: Chapter 2: Sign in or try the demo
x: Open Preferences and choose Sign Out under Account. This removes the token from your device. To withdraw access on the server too, remove Polylogue from the authorized apps in your Mastodon account settings on the web.

On iPad and Mac the sidebar sits beside the content. On iPhone it is its own screen; choose an item, and use the back button to return. When you open a post, profile, hashtag or article, a round back button at the top left returns you to the list. On Mac you can also open Preferences from the app menu, with ⌘,.

Home holds posts and boosts from accounts and hashtags you follow. Local holds public posts from accounts on your own server. Federated holds public posts your server knows about, from your server and others. It is your server's view, not everything that exists. Choose the information button in the toolbar for a reminder of what a timeline contains.

While Polylogue is active, the open timeline checks for new posts about once a minute. You can also choose Refresh or pull down. Scroll to the end to load older posts. Some servers turn off their Local or Federated feeds. Polylogue then tells you the server has disabled that feed.

Under each post are Reply, Boost, Favorite, Bookmark and, when the post has a web address, Share. Tap the post or its time to open the conversation. Tap the name or picture to open the profile. A small symbol beside the time marks a post that is not fully public.

c: Chapter 5: Conversations, warnings, polls and media
x: Tap a post to see it with the posts before it and the replies after it. A server only knows some replies, so another server may show more. An edited post is marked Edited.

x: A post with a content warning shows only the warning. Choose Show to read it and Hide to fold it again.

c: Chapter 5: Conversations, warnings, polls and media
x: Media marked sensitive is covered, both in timeline lists and in conversations. Choose Sensitive media to reveal it. In lists, the previews are not loaded until you do.

c: Chapter 5: Conversations, warnings, polls and media
x: Select your choice, or several if the poll allows it, and choose Vote. Results appear after you vote or when the poll ends. Some polls hide totals until they end.

c: Chapter 5: Conversations, warnings, polls and media
x: Open the conversation to see media at full width and to play video. Tap an image to view it on its own and to translate text in it.

Explore has four sections: Posts, Hashtags, News and For You. They show what your own server reports as trending, and accounts it suggests with a short reason. Choose a hashtag to see its posts, a news item to read it inside Polylogue, or Follow beside a suggested account. A section can be empty if your server has nothing trending or does not offer it.

Type at least two characters. Results are grouped into People, Hashtags and Posts. Your server decides what can be found. Searching for a full address, such as @name@server.example, can find someone on another server. A hashtag in search results opens its web page.

Open Preferences and choose Reading language under Translation. You can choose Arabic, Chinese, Dutch, English, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Turkish or Ukrainian. Polylogue starts with your device's language.

Translate timeline posts automatically is on at first. Posts in other languages are replaced by their translation, with a line saying which language and how it was translated. Turn it off to see a Translate from… button under such posts instead. Choose Show original or Show translation to switch. Content warnings and poll choices are shown as written.

s: When Apple cannot translate a pair
x: Which languages work depends on Apple's Translation framework on your device, and your device may ask to download a language first. Bridge unsupported Apple pairs through English, on at first, translates into English and then into your language, both on device. Some nuance may be lost. If no route works, you can use AI translation, described in Chapter 9. Apple Translation does not work in the iOS Simulator.
Polylogue keeps recent translations so they appear again quickly. Choose Clear Translation Cache in Preferences to remove them, including image text.

Open the conversation and tap the image. Choose Translate Image Text. Polylogue downloads the image, recognizes its text on your device with Apple Vision, and translates it. Use Show Detected Text to check what was recognized, Copy to copy the text shown, and Hide or Show to move the panel out of the way. Results are cached.

No readable text was found in this image means nothing was recognized. If Apple cannot translate the language and you have set up AI translation, you can try the provider. Only the recognized text is sent, never the image, and only for public and quiet public posts.
You do not need this to use Polylogue. You need your own account and API key with a provider, which may charge you.

In Preferences, turn on Enable AI translation fallback. Choose a Provider: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini or OpenAI-compatible. Enter your key and choose Save API Key. Choose Load Available Models and pick one, or type a model name. For OpenAI-compatible services, enter the full HTTPS chat-completions address. Provider status shows Ready when everything is in place. Each provider keeps its own key and model. Remove Key deletes the key for the selected provider.

By default Apple Translation comes first, and a Translate with AI button appears only when Apple cannot do the job. Automatically use AI for unsupported languages translates those posts without waiting for you. It becomes available after you have confirmed an AI translation with the current provider. Use AI assistant before Apple Translation makes AI the first choice.

Only public and quiet public posts and replies. Followers-only and direct posts are never sent. Polylogue asks you to confirm the first time it sends a post, image text or a reply to a provider. It asks again when you change to another provider, or to another OpenAI-compatible address. After you confirm, it does not ask again for that one. See the privacy policy.
Open a timeline and choose New Post. Write up to 500 characters. Choose the audience, and add a content warning, media or a poll if you like. Choose Publish.
Audience Who sees the post Public Everyone, including public timelines Quiet Public Everyone, but not listed in public timelines Followers Your followers and people you mention
Choose Add Content Warning and write a short subject. Attached media is then hidden automatically.

New posts take their audience, language, sensitive media and warning settings from your server. See Server Posting Defaults in Preferences. If you choose Cancel, your text is kept and restored next time, marked Draft restored. Only the text is saved, not media, polls or the warning.

Choose Reply under a post, or Reply across languages in a conversation. The reply starts with the addresses of the author and of everyone the post mentions, except you, so they are notified. Remove any you do not want to include. Write your reply after them, in your reading language. The addresses at the start are not translated. Check Reply language. It starts as the language of the post. Choose Preview. Compare your original with the translation, and edit the translation as needed. Choose Publish. When the reply language is your reading language, there is no preview and you publish directly. The reply language list also includes Hungarian. Mastodon keeps one language version of a post. Others see only what you publish; Polylogue keeps your original on your device. Content warnings and poll choices are published exactly as you typed them.

Apple Translation is used when it can. If the post you are answering was translated by AI, the same provider and model translate your reply. AI is also used when Apple does not support the pair and you have AI set up. The first time a reply would go to a provider you have not confirmed, Polylogue asks. Choose Send and Translate, or Cancel to keep the text on your device.
A translation can be longer than your original. Edit it down to 500 characters, or choose Shorten with AI if AI made the translation.

A reply keeps the privacy of the conversation. You cannot make a followers-only conversation public. Private replies are never sent to an AI service; if Apple cannot translate one, write it in the other language yourself.
A post can have media or a poll, not both.

Choose Add Photos or Video, then your Photos library or your files. You can attach up to four. Use Describe this media for accessibility for each one, and Mark media as sensitive if needed. Remove an item with the button beside it. Large files take longer: Polylogue uploads them when you publish and waits for the server to process them.
Choose Add Poll, enter two to four choices, and set the duration, from 5 minutes to 7 days. You can Allow multiple choices and Hide totals until the poll ends. A poll needs post text too.

x: Open your profile from the bottom of the sidebar and choose Edit Profile. You can change: your display name and biography; up to four profile fields, such as a website or pronouns; Require approval for new followers; Show this profile in discovery; This is an automated account. Choose Save. Changing your picture or header image is not available in Polylogue; use your server's website.

Polylogue has no account of its own, no ads and no analytics. It connects to your Mastodon server, to the places that host images, video and articles you view, and to an AI provider only if you set one up.

Your sign-in token and API keys are in the Keychain. Settings, drafts, your originals of translated replies and translation caches are in the app's storage. Cached translations can include text from private posts, translated on your device. Signing out does not erase drafts, caches or API keys. Use Clear Translation Cache and Remove Key if you want them gone. Read the full privacy policy.
Enter just the server address, such as mastodon.social. Check that the server opens in your web browser. After allowing access, let the browser open Polylogue.

Check Reading language and that the post is in a different language. Accept any language download your device offers. Turn on bridging through English. For languages Apple does not support, set up AI translation.
Check Provider status. Confirm the key, model and, for compatible services, the HTTPS address. An error from the provider is shown under the post. Private and direct posts are never translated by AI.
